formula: genx ~ 1 + (1 | country)
notes: MISSING SUSPECTED: country is the empty text on 47 of 10,964 rows, which no code can declare. Second reading of a flat table. Bayes Rules! (Johnson, Ott and Dogucu 2022, chapter 8, bayesrulesbook.com/chapter-8) estimates the share of artists who are Gen X or younger, genx, on moma_sample, 'A random sample of 100 artists' of this collection (excluded as a subset of moma), by a Beta(4, 6) prior and a Binomial likelihood without predictors; a model on a subset documents the table, so genx is the response. country ('country of origin') indexes the nationalities the artists repeat within, most holding several artists, so it groups the rows as HSAUR3 Forbes2000's country groups its companies; the random intercept is the reader's proposal, inferred from the column, and the book's model names no grouping, so published_model is no. birth is ignored, since genx is 'born during 1965 or after'; gender and department classify the artists and stay out of the documented model. artist repeats over the departments its works appear in: 1,554 of the 9,069 artists hold 2 to 5 rows each, 10,964 rows in all, which the package's data-raw/moma.R builds; the extra department rows repeat the artist's genx with count and the acquisition years mostly missing. The repeats are no independent artists, and artist carries no random effect, genx being constant within it, so the fit takes the 9,071 rows with a count, one per artist (fits_preparation.csv). Outside check: notes corrected, the row stands.

RULE GAP: svo, the social value orientation angle the script computes from the six slider items SV03 to SV08 through Murphy et al.'s payoff lookup matrix (the arctangent of the mean other and self payoffs), is no column and no closed expression of them, so the formula names it as the script does; the script also reverses the three ratings of the attention check 'attend corona parties', recodes -9 as missing and drops the participants who always answered at an extreme, steps no cell states. Analysis.Rmd numbers the rows vpn = 1:n() (Unnamed: 0 holds the same numbers, ignored) and pivots RD02_, RD03_ and RD04_ by names_sep '_' into self (self-protection), public (public protection) and freq (how often the behavior is shown) by behavior 1 to 17, labeled by List_behaviors.csv, the stack filed here. It rescales the 1 to 101 sliders to 0 to 1 and fits glmmTMB(freqScaled ~ svo + self*public + self:svo + public:svo + (self|behavior) + (1|behavior) + (1|vpn), family = beta with logit link), freqScaled = freq * 0.999 + 0.0005 so no value is 0 or 1, filed here without the second (1|behavior), which repeats the intercept of (self|behavior). The paper's Table 2 reports a beta GLMM with intercepts only for behavior and participant.
